item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 11:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Erik Williams)
Mike Yastrzemski capped a four-run sixth inning with a three-run homer, and the visiting Atlanta Braves clinched the National League East with a 4-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Sunday.
The Braves swept the three-game interleague series and claimed their seventh division pennant over the last nine seasons. Yastrzemski was the last of four batters to reach safely against Astros left-handed reliever Bryan King (3-6), who didn't record a single out and exited after allowing Yastrzemski's 12th homer of the season.
Jose Altuve and Yainer Diaz homered for the spiraling Astros, who will enter the final week of the regular season one game behind the Texas Rangers in the American League West.
Astros starter Hunter Brown allowed just three singles and two walks over five shutout innings. Braves starter Martin Perez navigated traffic, allowing just one run on six hits and two walks in 4 1/3 innings.
Rays 5, Red Sox 1
Tampa Bay's Jonny DeLuca and Chandler Simpson drove in two runs apiece during a four-run first inning, Victor Mesa Jr. homered and the Rays defeated visiting Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla.
With the win, the Rays completed their final regular-season homestand with an 8-1 record and wrapped their home schedule with a major league-best 55-26 mark.
Trevor Story homered, and Roman Anthony and Caleb Durbin each went 2-for-4 for the Red Sox, who managed just six hits while losing their second straight game.
Pirates 4, Royals 3
Rafael Flores Jr. belted a go-ahead two-run homer in the eighth inning to cap Pittsburgh's three-game sweep over visiting Kansas City. With the win, the Pirates improved to 14-6 in their last 20 games.
Oneil Cruz went deep to lead off the fourth inning and Spencer Horwitz had an RBI single in the sixth for Pittsburgh. Carmen Mlodzinski earned the win after allowing two runs on three hits in three innings.
Vinnie Pasquantino had a pinch-hit two-run homer for the Royals, who have lost four in a row and seven of their past eight games.
Phillies 7, Mets 2
Cristopher Sanchez tossed 6 1/3 solid innings and earned the victory for visiting Philadelphia, which earned a much-needed win over New York.
Luis Arraez was 1-for-4 with two RBIs for the Phillies. Justin Crawford provided insurance in the eighth with a bases-clearing triple off Kodai Senga. Sanchez (18-6) gave up two runs on six hits. Philadelphia sits four games ahead of the Arizona Diamondbacks in the race for the final National League wild card.
Bo Bichette homered for the Mets, who dropped their home finale for the third time in four years, while Brett Baty had a pinch-hit run-scoring single in the seventh. Francisco Alvarez and A.J. Ewing each singled twice.
Cubs 9, Reds 1
Pete Crow-Armstrong tied the major league lead with his 45th home run, and David Peterson held host Cincinnati to one run on three hits in six innings in Chicago's win.
Crow-Armstrong was 3-for-5 with two RBIs, three runs, his 30th double and his 38th stolen base. He matched Philadelphia's Kyle Schwarber at 45 homers, and he became the first center fielder in history with 40 home runs, 30 doubles and 30 steals in a season.
Michael Conforto and Seiya Suzuki also homered for the Cubs. JJ Bleday hit a home run for the Reds, who have dropped three of four.
Cardinals 5, Nationals 3
Leo Bernal's two-run home run capped a three-run eighth inning, and St. Louis rallied for a win against visiting Washington to salvage the finale of the three-game series.
Ivan Herrera tied it 3-3 with one out when he hit his second solo homer of the day. Luis Gastelum (5-3) pitched a scoreless inning for the win. Jose Fermin had two hits for the Cardinals, who had lost four straight.
CJ Abrams homered, and Daylen Lile had a double and a single for Washington, which had won six of seven.
Mariners 2, Rockies 1
Kade Anderson threw seven scoreless innings, allowing just three hits in the longest outing of his rookie season, and visiting Seattle stayed alive in the postseason race with a win over Colorado in Denver.
Dominic Canzone had two hits and two RBIs for Seattle, which gained a game on the Texas Rangers in the AL West. Closer Andres Munoz left the game in the ninth with an apparent right arm injury.
Hunter Goodman's 39th home run of the season couldn't prevent Colorado from moving within one loss of its fourth consecutive 100-loss season.
Blue Jays 7, Rangers 2
Nathan Lukes and Charles McAdoo each had two RBIs to lead Toronto to a win over Texas in Arlington, Texas.
Kazuma Okamoto broke a 2-2 deadlock with an RBI single in the fifth and gave the Blue Jays a lead they would never relinquish as they remained three games back of the final AL wild-card spot. Spencer Arrighetti (9-9) picked up the win, allowing two runs in 2 1/3 innings during a bullpen game.
Jake Burger delivered the Rangers' lone runs on a game-tying two-run homer in the fourth. Jacob deGrom (11-10) had a shaky outing, giving up three runs with five hits in 4 1/3 innings for Texas, which maintained its one-game lead in the AL West despite the defeat.
Brewers 3, Orioles 0
Jacob Misiorowski set the tone with three shutout innings and Milwaukee blanked host Baltimore for the second game in a row to complete a three-game sweep and set a franchise record for regular-season victories.
William Contreras homered, and Cooper Pratt provided two run-scoring singles with two outs. Milwaukee is two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the National League. Misiorowski's ERA dipped to 1.86.
The Orioles further damaged their fading playoff hopes, losing the first three games of the homestand to fall five games back of the Chicago White Sox for the final American League wild-card spot. Colton Cowser had two of Baltimore's four hits. Orioles starter Brandon Young (9-5) was charged with two runs in six innings.
Diamondbacks 8, Yankees 4
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and Arizona kept its slim National League wild-card chances alive with a victory over New York in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1/3 scoreless innings. The D-backs remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies with six to play.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Twins 8, Angels 0
Dean Kremer allowed one hit over six innings and Alan Roden went 3-for-5 with a home run and four RBIs as Minnesota earned a split of its four-game series with Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Josh Bell had three hits, a walk, two RBIs and a run while Brooks Lee also had three hits and scored three times for Minnesota, which finished with 13 hits. Kremer (4-5) allowed just a fourth-inning leadoff single to Vaughn Grissom.
Ryan Johnson (5-9) suffered the loss for Los Angeles, which finished the 2026 season with a 34-47 home record.
Guardians 1, Athletics 0
Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings to lift Cleveland past the visiting Athletics.
Williams (14-8) gave up only three hits while throwing 63 of 89 pitches for strikes. Steven Kwan had three hits and Cade Smith earned his 39th save as the Guardians swept the series and remain atop the American League Central.
A's starter Jack Perkins (3-12) gave up five hits and one run in six innings. Zack Gelof had two of the team's six hits as the Athletics suffered their sixth straight loss
Dodgers 3, Giants 1
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and Los Angeles completed a three-game sweep of visiting San Francisco.
Tommy Edman homered for the Dodgers, who trailed 1-0 after one inning before Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit with nine strikeouts over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings.
Jung Hoo Lee and Victor Bericoto singled for the only hits for the Giants, who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record. Sam Hentges (1-7) allowed a pair of one-out singles in the seventh before Hernandez's double for a 2-1 edge.
Padres 7, Marlins 3
Jake Cronenworth homered twice and knocked in a season-high five runs while Fernando Tatis Jr. also homered as host San Diego polished off a three-game sweep and finished 6-0 against Miami this season.
The Padres won their fifth straight game and are 13-1 in their last 14 games. Walker Buehler (9-6) worked 6 2/3 innings, allowing three hits and three runs.
Sandy Alcantara (13-11) absorbed the loss for the Marlins after permitting eight hits and four runs over six innings. Alcantara is winless in his last eight starts.
White Sox 8, Tigers 1
Chase Meidroth hit a two-run homer for Chicago and Sam Antonacci's two-run double highlighted a 2-for-4 performance as the White Sox waited through a rain delay of nearly four hours and played in wet, blustery conditions to beat Detroit.
Five pitchers held the Tigers to six hits and five walks as Detroit was limited to a single run for the third time in the series. Huascar Brazoban (6-2), reinstated prior to the game from the 15-day injured list (left lat strain), pitched for the first time since Aug. 24. He allowed a hit in one inning to get his first victory with the White Sox.
Tigers starter Troy Melton (8-5) allowed four runs in 3 2/3 innings, giving up four hits before exiting with a trainer. Detroit pitchers allowed eight walks, with White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas (1-for-2) drawing three of them. Eduardo Valencia went 3-for-4 for the Tigers, who were eliminated from postseason contention.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [thetimes-tribune.com] SWB RAILRIDERS: End of an era for franchise’s nickname
item.dc:creator: Scott Walsh
item.description: MOOSIC — Edinson Duran became the unlikely answer to a trivia question. item.content:encoded:
MOOSIC — Edinson Duran became the unlikely answer to a trivia question.
Sunday’s season finale between the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders and Jacksonville Jumbo Shrimp at PNC Field was canceled due to rain and wet grounds. That meant Saturday night’s game was the last one featuring the RailRiders nickname. The team is rebranding and expected to announce the new identity in November.
So when people ask who was the winning pitcher in the final game of the RailRiders era, it isn’t a top prospect like Elmer Rodriguez or an ace like Brendan Beck. It is Duran, a catcher who spent more time on the development list this season than the active roster.
Whenever the RailRiders would need to use a position player to save arms in the bullpen, they would go to Duran. He’s done it eight times in the past two seasons, including six this season.
In the top of the 10th inning Saturday night, Justin Topa struck out the first two batters with the automatic runner on second base. However, with the count 2-1 to Logan Driscoll, Topa reached his pitch limit. With no other options, manager Shelley Duncan called upon Duran. The 24-year old from Venezuela walked Driscoll, then walked Gage Miller to load the bases, but got Johnny Olmstead to fly out to center fielder Duke Ellis to end the inning. The RailRiders won in the bottom of the 10th, 6-5, when automatic runner Yanquiel Fernandez scored from third base on a wild pitch, making Duran the winning pitcher.
“It was really exciting for Duran to come in and do what he did,” RailRiders reliever Eric Reyzelman said. “It’s fun, kind of reminds you why you play this game. Technically, we had nothing on the line playoff-wise. But we did not want to leave this place without a win.”
And so the RailRiders’ final ride has pulled into the station. The team finished 78-68 overall (37-37 first half, 41-31 second half). Its all-time record wound up 1,028 wins and 834 losses.
From the first pitch by Vidal Nuño to Pawtucket’s Brock Holt on April 4, 2013, to the last one Saturday night — Jacksonville’s Stephen Jones’ wild pitch with Kenedy Corona batting — a lot of memorable moments happened in between.
Six times the RailRiders made the playoffs. Three times they lost in the International League championship series (2017, 2018, 2025). But in 2016, they defeated the Gwinnett Braves in four games to capture the IL title, then beat the Pacific Coast League champion El Paso Chihuahuas to claim the Triple-A national championship.
Many notable players have worn a RailRiders uniform.
Hall of Famer Derek Jeter spent seven games on a rehab assignment in early July 2013 while recovering from a broken ankle. During his time here, it became a daily game to see where he was spotted in downtown Scranton.
Later that month, Alex Rodriguez played three games here while coming back from offseason hip surgery. He hit a two-run home run in the second at-bat of his first game.
Curtis Granderson and D.J. LeMahieu were other notable Yankees who rehabbed here over the years. This season, pitchers Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodon and outfielder Cody Bellinger had rehab stints.
Current Yankees slugger Aaron Judge played 154 games with the RailRiders in 2015 and 2016 and five more games on a rehab assignment in 2019. He totaled 28 home runs and 95 RBIs. Prospects such as Gary Sanchez, Anthony Volpe and George Lombard Jr. spent time here.
“A lot of great players have played for the RailRiders,” said Beck, who wound up leading the International League in earned-run average (2.93), strikeouts (151), innings (135.1), WHIP (1.06) and opponents’ batting average (.210). “To be the last ones to do it is fun. The future is exciting as well. Looking forward to starting something new next year. But to be the team to end the RailRiders dynasty on a comeback win with a good crowd at home is a lot of fun. Definitely a fun day at the office.”
When Duncan played in Scranton/Wilkes-Barre from 2007-09, the team was known as the Yankees. But in his four seasons as manager, the term “RailRiders” has come to mean a lot to him.
“I just always think about the character of every team that I’ve had,” said Duncan, whose record as RailRiders manager is 327-195. “I’ve been lucky to be a part of some good groups that fought all the way to the end. Some good memories and some good relationships. Each year has been a different team and each year has been very special.”
Clint Frazier was a top prospect who played 213 games for the RailRiders from 2016-19 before a severe concussion and lingering symptoms ultimately sidetracked his career. Because of his frequent shuttling between the minors and the majors, he proclaimed himself a “RailRider for Life.”
He made an appearance at Saturday night’s game, signing autographs for fans and throwing out the ceremonial first pitch.
“It was me being a little facetious,” Frazier said. “I think it started around the time I got optioned to the minor leagues in 2019. I was doing relatively well at the big-league level. When I came down here, there was something in the media about September roster expansion and the Yankees were kind of vague on whether I going to be coming back. I remember parking in a parking garage and seeing this sign that said ‘Scranton Life’ and I was like, ‘Dude, I don’t want to be a Yankee. I want to be a RailRider for Life.’ It was a facetious comment and I ended up running with it because it was kind of funny. People obviously took notice to it because I put it on my Twitter bio and it’s been there for like 10 years.”
Frazier was a little surprised and a bit disappointed when he heard the team was rebranding and retiring the RailRiders nickname.
“I’m not a part of the Yankees anymore and I’m not here in Scranton,” Frazier said. “So if they want to rebrand or it’s something the fans want, you give them it. But other than that, I was kind of like, ‘Damn, I guess I won’t be a RailRider anymore. I’ll be whatever they are.’ But I’ll still be a RailRider at heart.”
The nickname has not only meant something to players.
Kristina Knight has been with the team for 20 seasons. She started as an intern with the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre Red Barons, then worked in tickets sales and group sales, sponsor servicing and currently is senior director of partnership management and marketing.
“I think it was extra special because it was a community-thought name,” Knight said. “We surveyed the community and did the poll of submitting your ideas. So I like to think it was the community’s name, which was extra special within itself. The reason we went away from the Yankees name was to give the area more ownership of the team here. I think it did that for sure.
“When we were the Yankees, it was very nice and obviously nice to be included in the Yankees family. But the RailRiders was our very own name and gave our own identity in the minor-league baseball world.”
When the new nickname is announced in November, Knight believes that the community will accept it as well.
“I think it will be as well-received and special to the community,” Knight said. “We are trying to make sure it reflects everything in this area that we find very special and attractive about our area and try to make it a highlight to the nation.”

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

21 Sep 2026, 04:55 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Nolan Arenado hit his third grand slam of the season to cap a five-run fifth and the Arizona Diamondbacks kept their slim National League wild card chances alive with an 8-4 victory over the New York Yankees on Sunday in Phoenix.
Geraldo Perdomo had two hits and two RBIs and five Arizona relievers limited the Yankees to three hits in 6 1-3 scoreless innings as the D-backs scored the final seven runs for their major league-leading 47th comeback win.
Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones homered for the Yankees, who fell six games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East. The Yankees lead the American League with 216 homers. Lombard had two hits.
Lars Nootbaar and Gabriel Moreno had two hits and scored twice and Ketel Marte had two hits for the Diamondbacks, who have won two straight games.
The D-backs (82-74) remained five games behind NL wild-card leaders Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres (both 87-69) and four behind the Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) with six to play.
The D-backs would lose a tiebreaker to the Cubs, and tiebreakers against the Padres and Phillies have yet to be determined. The D-backs end the season with three games at Colorado and the final three at San Diego.
Justin Martinez (3-0), the second Arizona reliever to follow Corbin Burnes, struck out two in the fifth for the victory.
The Yankees lost their second straight after winning four of five.
Nootbaar started the D-backs' five-run fifth with a one-out double off Yankees starter Will Warren. Marte singled and Moreno walked to load the bases. Brent Headrick (7-4) entered and struck out Perdomo before walking Corbin Carroll to force in a run.
Arenado followed with his 381-foot homer into the Arizona bullpen for a 6-4 edge. He has five homers in his last 10 games and is tied with Houston's Yordan Alvarez for the major league lead in grand slams.
Perdomo tripled in a run and scored on Carroll's single in a two-run seventh.
The D-backs took a 1-0 lead in the first on singles by Nootbaar, Marte and Perdomo. Warren gave up six hits and four runs in 4 1/3 innings, with three walks and four strikeouts.
Ramos, Lombard and Jones homered four batters apart in a four-run third off Burnes for a 4-1 lead. Ramos homered with two outs before Luis Garcia Jr. singled and Lombard and Jones hit back-to-back shots. Lombard's went an estimated 424 feet. Jones' went 448.Burnes gave up four runs and five hits, with two walks and two strikeouts in 2 2/3 innings. He has given up nine runs and five homers in 10 1-3 innings of three starts since returning after a 15-month absence after Tommy John surgery.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees’ chances of winning the AL East are on life support.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Of greater concern is whether their bullpen meltdown Sunday was just a bad day or represents cracks emerging in a heavily worked unit.
Brent Headrick served up a grand slam to Nolan Arenado in the fifth inning, flipping the game on its head and all but wrapping up the Yankees’ spot in the AL wild-card series next week after an 8-4 loss to the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
By dropping the series finale, a game they once led 4-1, the Yankees (89-66) fell to six games back of the Rays with seven to play.
They will welcome the Rays to Yankee Stadium on Tuesday for a four-game showdown, needing a sweep to stay alive in the division race. One win by the Rays in The Bronx will secure them the AL East title.
The Yankees would then turn their attention to securing the top AL wild card, ending Sunday leading the Red Sox by 5 ¹/₂ games, though Aaron Judge’s questionable status for that series because of a calf strain looms over everything.
In the meantime, Sunday’s loss — on the heels of Saturday’s walk-off win by the Diamondbacks (82-74) — was another regrettable one after third-inning home runs by Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. and Spencer Jones had staked them to a 4-1 lead.
In the bottom of the fifth, Will Warren loaded the bases with one out, at which point Aaron Boone called on reliable lefty Headrick for his 79th appearance of the season — the second most in the majors.
Before Sunday, Headrick had inherited 50 runners this season and allowed only five of them to score.
But after striking out the first batter he faced, Headrick walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run, which brought Arenado to the plate.
Shop Yankees Merch
Arenado crushed Headrick’s 2-0 fastball just to the left of the left field foul pole, but then straightened it out on the very next pitch (another fastball), clobbering a grand slam to put the Diamondbacks ahead 6-4.
The Diamondbacks later added a pair of insurance runs off John Schreiber in the seventh inning, the first earned runs Schreiber has allowed as a Yankee.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could activate Jazz Chisholm Jr. as soon as Tuesday, raising questions about Anthony Volpe's role.
Nothing is set yet, manager Aaron Boone said Sunday, according to New York Daily News reporter Gary Phillips. The update came before the Yankees played the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix.
Chisholm sprained his right thumb Sept. 8. The Yankees recalled Volpe, 25, from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre on Sept. 10. They had optioned him in early August after promoting shortstop George Lombard Jr.
Volpe has played second base since then and has produced remarkable numbers.
Through Saturday, he has gone 9-for-31 in nine games since his recall. That is a .290 average with a .333 on-base percentage, a .452 slugging percentage and a .785 OPS.
He has one home run, two doubles, seven RBIs and four runs scored. Volpe has walked twice, struck out four times and stolen four bases without being caught.
Anthony Volpe's Future Is Still Not Known
Volpe could also see time at third base in the coming days. Boone fielded a question about using Volpe there, Phillips reported.
"We'll see," Boone said. "First things first, getting Jazz back and then we'll figure out as the week unfolds how I want to play it."
Volpe also addressed the idea, Phillips reported.
He said the Yankees have not talked to him about playing third base before the regular season ends. He said he felt comfortable there the few times he played third base in the minors.
At Triple-A, Volpe made 19 starts at second base, 15 at shortstop and three at third base.
Chisholm is batting .232 with 19 home runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games this season.
The Yankees open their final homestand Tuesday with a doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays. They entered Sunday at 89-65.
Trent Grisham is Out for the Regular Season
Boone said the Yankees do not expect to activate Trent Grisham before the regular season ends, MLB.com's Bryan Hoch reported.
Grisham could still be on the playoff roster, Boone said.
The New York Post's Greg Joyce reported that roster complications are part of the reason. The Yankees would have to send a player down and could not recall him for 10 days, Joyce reported.
Joyce contrasted that with activating Grisham directly onto the playoff roster.
Grisham has been on the 10-day injured list since Sept. 5 with a Grade 2 right hamstring strain. He left a Sept. 4 game against the San Diego Padres in the third inning. It is his second right hamstring strain of the season.
Grisham is batting .211 with 18 home runs and 59 RBIs this season. The 29-year-old will be a free agent after the season.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees Face Anthony Volpe Decision After Jazz Chisholm Jr. News appeared first on HEAVY.

Nolan Arenado hit a fifth-inning grand slam off Brent Headrick as the Yankees absorbed an 8-4 loss on Sunday afternoon at Chase Field. With seven games remaining, New York trails Tampa Bay by six games in the division race.

Will Warren allowed four runs on six hits and three walks over 4 1/3 innings. Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed that Warren will draw one more start during the regular season, set to face the Orioles, before transitioning to a bullpen role during the playoffs.
Headrick issued a bases-loaded walk to Corbin Carroll, then saw Arenado crush a drive just foul down the left-field line before pouncing on the next pitch for a grand slam that put Arizona ahead.

item.content:encoded:
In the final game and rubber match of their three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), the Yankees (89-66) coughed up an early lead to lose 8-4.
Here are the takeaways...
-- Will Warren got the nod to start the game, and delivered a solid outing... until the fifth inning. Up to that point, Warren had allowed one earned run - an RBI single in the first inning by Diamondbacks shortstop Geraldo Perdomo - and struck out four batters through four full innings. The Yankees entered the fifth inning leading 4-1 (thanks to home runs from Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr., and Spencer Jones), but after Warren surrendered two hits and a walk to load the bases with just one man out, he was pulled in favor of left-handed reliever Brent Headrick.
-- Headrick struck out Perdomo to record the second out, but he couldn't close the door on the frame, issuing a free pass to Corbin Carroll to bring in one run before surrendering a grand slam to Nolan Arenado which gave Arizona a 6-4 lead.
-- Of those five earned runs surrendered in the fifth, three were attributed to Warren, and two to Headrick.
-- New York's right-handed reliever John Schreiber allowed two more runs in the seventh inning, surrendering a triple to Perdomo and a single to Carroll which brought the shortstop home. For Arizona, former Yankee Jonathan Loáisiga recorded the final six outs, facing the minimum six batters without allowing a run to wrap up the 8-4 loss.
Game MVP: Nolan Arenado
Arenado's grand slam flipped the game on its head, and the massive momentum-shifting blast gave the Snakes a lead they wouldn't relinquish.
Highlights
What's next
The Yankees travel back home on Monday and will kick off a pivotal three game series against the AL East divisional leading Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday at 1:05 p.m.
Of course, now 6.0 games back of Tampa Bay for first place in the AL East with just seven regular season games remaining, the Yankees need a miracle to win the division.
Carlos Rodón (2.95 ERA, 1.13 WHIP in 76.1 IP) is set to take the mound for the Yankees.
The Rays will send out Nick Martinez (2.94 ERA, 1.07 WHIP in 171.1 IP).

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Brian Cashman foolishly built a Yankees roster that couldn't support Aaron Judge's return
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello

item.content:encoded:
From June 1 through the August 3 deadline, the New York Yankees were hurting for offense. The club ranked 28th during that span in OPS with a .672 mark. They were 26th in runs scored with 214, an average of 3.96 per game during that 54-game period. The Yankees collectively slashed a putrid .221/.283/.389.
As a result, Brian Cashman went out and bolstered the offense. He acquired Heliot Ramos, who was brutal at the start of his tenure in New York, but has bounced back over the past three weeks. Ramos, though, was an upgrade on the margins as a platoon bat brought into mash lefties. The real get was former Washington Nationals first baseman Luis Garcia Jr.
Garcia Jr. has looked like a budding star, so this next part is tough. He joined an already crowded first base-DH rotation that includes a fringe MVP candidate in Ben Rice and a former MVP who still plays like one against lefties, Paul Goldschmidt, with a 1.006 OPS this season against southpaws.
It made sense, except for one gigantic looming development. The Yankees were expecting to get Aaron Judge back before the end of the season, who would have a much greater impact on New York's offensive output than any external addition could have by a wide margin.
That created a situation that when Judge returned after missing over three months of action, he'd immediately have to jump back in to right field. The Yankees were unable to protect his body and easy him back in at DH thanks to the logjam Cashman created, and as a result, Judge is heading back to the IL after just seven games back. Now, his status for the playoffs is in peril.
Brian Cashman's lack of trade deadline vision put Aaron Judge and the Yankees' World Series hopes at risk
First, a caveat. Judge could have wound up with a calf injury even if he wasn't playing right field. We can get into whether or not he needed more time to ramp up and was brought back too fast, but that's a discussion for another day.
The fact of the matter is that Cashman went out at the deadline and reconstructed the roster in such a way that Judge could only play right field upon his return. That was a mistake.
Now, the market wasn't exactly flush with options, but with some creativity and a willingness to be bold, Cashman could have still completed the necessary task of upgrading the offense while ensuring Judge could be protected by being inserted into the DH spot upon activation.
For example, rather than relying on George Lombard Jr. to man shortstop and provide a spark, he could have gone out and gotten an established young star at the position like Zach Neto or CJ Abrams. Neither player moved at the deadline, but for the right package, they would have. It might have cost Lombard Jr. to get it done, but as we've seen sometimes holding on to even the best prospects can end poorly.
Another lever Cashman could've pulled would've been flexing the franchise's financial might and absorbing Rafael Devers' contract. Yes, Devers just underwent season-ending core muscle surgery, but his blistering .275/.375/.611 second-half performance would have at least bridged the gap until Judge was ready, and perhaps he wouldn't have suffered the same fate had he been dealt here.
Devers has played mostly first base and DH, but while he's not a great third baseman, that's where he has the most experience, and he could've benefited from playing next to the rangy Lombard Jr. Maybe not an ideal solution, but it would've solved the logjam.
Lastly, he could have thought outside the box and beat the Dodgers offer for Tarik Skubal. This wouldn't have helped the offense, but hey, if you struggle to score, you can still win if you make it even harder for your opponent to scratch runs across. In the meantime, the coaching staff could try to figure out why the bats had been so putrid yet hit the third-most homers in MLB (76) during that otherwise horrendous 54-game stretch.
At the end of the day, Cashman did what he always does and went out and got the controllable player with projection over the established star in order to keep his prospect cost down. As a result, he created a logjam that put unnecessary risk on his three-time MVP. If Judge isn't ready in time for the start of October baseball, it will be a devastating blow to the Yankees' World Series aspirations, and it was all completely avoidable.

The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we'll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who's finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he'll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn't totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He's always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn't have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We've seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who'll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night's hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.

Location: Chase Field, Phoenix, AZ
First pitch: 4:10 pm ET
TV broadcast: YES, DBACKS.TV
Radio broadcast: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 (NYY), ESPN 620 AM, La Campesina 101.9 FM & 860 AM (AZ)

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] The only Yankees position without multiple Silver Slugger winners should send message to front office
item.dc:creator: Stephen Parello
item.description: The New York Yankees aren't nicknamed the Bronx Bombers for no reason. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees aren't nicknamed the Bronx Bombers for no reason. For that reason, they've been well represented in the Louisville Slugger Silver Slugger Awards throughout the years. The Yankees have multiple representatives at every position except for one: shortstop.
This is in part because the award was first introduced in 1980, meaning that franchise greats and champions like Phil Rizzuto and Frank Crosetti missed the boat by a large margin. Another mitigating factor is that New York had one player dominate the position for much of the Silver Slugger era. That, of course, is Derek Jeter, who had a stranglehold on the position for the better part of two decades, taking home the award five times himself.
But while it seems like yesterday, Jeter's last big league season was in 2014. Since then, the position has looked pretty bleak. From 2015 through the present day, the Yankees have gotten a .715 OPS out of the position, which ranks 15th in the majors during that span.
That number includes the Didi Gregorius years, which included some very fine performances. Gregorius hit 97 homers in pinstripes over five seasons, while slashing .269/.313/.446. That's nothing to sneeze at, but he was never the AL's best hitter at the position during his time here.
Gregorius left following the 2019 season, and since then, things have been bleak. From 2020 onward, we have mostly been dealing with Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Anthony Volpe at short. In that time period, Yankees shortstops have produced a .668 OPS, ranking 26th in baseball.
The Yankees can't continue getting subpar offensive production out of the shortstop position
Right now, the hope for the future is George Lombard Jr. The club's top prospect got off to a hot start, but since then, he's cooled substantially. It's too early to write him off just yet, especially at just 21 years old. However, the Yankees can't afford to get into another Volpe-esque holding pattern where years go by and no material improvements are made.
That leaves the front office with an interesting conundrum. Shortstops who can hit and field don't grow on trees, and while Brian Cashman passed on a generational shortstop free-agent class to sign IKF to keep the seat warm for Volpe, he cannot afford to repeat the same lethargic approach to the position.
Ideally, Lombard Jr. snatches the job for the next 20 years with a strong finish to 2026, a postseason to remember, and a spring training that eliminates all doubt. Jeter met with the promising youngster to advise him on the responsibilities that lie ahead. Now we'll see if he took those lessons to heart.
But if we come to the conclusion of New York's 2026 campaign and haven't seen Lombard Jr. show signs that he can consistently rise to the occasion; the Yankees must be opportunistic when it comes to pursuing upgrades.
After being wrapped up in rumors at the trade deadline, it's thought that the Angels could revisit trade talks for Zach Neto in the offseason. Another possible scenario is that the Astros follow the Kyle Tucker path and trade Jeremy Peña this winter ahead of his final year of team control.
In an ideal situation, the Yankees could acquire a player like Neto or Peña while retaining Lombard Jr. to hedge their bets. Worst-case scenario: Lombard Jr. busts, and the team has a high-end veteran to man the position. Best-case scenario: they have to undertake some shuffling, but Lombard Jr. is a star, and the team is deeper and better for it.
What can't happen is the Yankees put all their eggs in the Lombard Jr. bucket, and then miss out on young stars in their prime and let the position languish for another half-decade. The time to wait and see is over, and the time to be bold is now.

item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the New York Yankees will finish their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix.
They are coming off a 5-3 loss on Saturday night.
That said, the series is tied up at 1-1 heading into the finale.
George Lombard Jr. Makes Honest Gerrit Cole Statement
On Friday, Gerrit Cole got the start.
He allowed just two earned runs in 6.0 innings.
After the game, George Lombard Jr. was asked about Cole (via YES Network).
Reporter: “Gerrit won a Cy Young in 2023 when you graduated from high school. What’s it like for you to play behind him?”
Lombard Jr.: “It’s awesome. Yeah. I’ve watched him dominate on the mound for as long as I can remember. It’s really cool to be on the same field as him.”
Looking At Lombard Jr.
Lombard Jr. was picked in the 1st round of the 2023 MLB Draft.
He made his MLB debut last month.
The 21-year-old is currently batting .227 with 29 hits, four home runs, 15 RBIs, 19 runs and two stolen bases in 36 games.
Looking At Cole
Cole has been one of the best pitchers in the recent era of baseball.
The former Cy Young Award winner is in the middle of his 6th season pitching for New York.
He has also had stops with the Houston Astros and Pittsburgh Pirates.
Right now, Cole is 9-9 with a 3.63 ERA in 21 starts.
Looking At The Yankees Right Now
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East with an 89-65 record in 154 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games (and are 47-33 in 80 games on the road).
On Tuesday, the Yankees will return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays in the Bronx.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Spencer Jones Da Un Buen Susto A Los Yankees Por Una Lesión, Ya Que El Césped Del Chase Field Le Ha Hecho Daño En El Talón
item.dc:creator: Sara Molnick

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees llegaron a Arizona con el objetivo de mantener su puesto en la postemporada, sin dejar de luchar por una oportunidad cada vez más lejana de ganar la División Este de la Liga Americana. Para el sábado por la noche, la clasificación ya no era más que una parte del problema.
El propio Chase Field se había convertido en algo con lo que Aaron Boone tenía que lidiar.
Nueva York llegaba al domingo con un balance de 89-65 tras perder por 5-3 en la última entrada ante los Diamondbacks, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay cuando solo quedan ocho partidos por disputar. Los Yankees seguían ocupando el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana, pero su margen para hacer frente a otra lesión se había reducido después de que Aaron Judge volviera a la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha.
Las decisiones de Boone del sábado reflejaron esa realidad. José Caballero fue titular en el centro del campo por segunda vez esta temporada. Cody Bellinger se quedó en la izquierda en lugar de cambiar de posición, a pesar de que tiene mucha experiencia jugando en el centro del campo. Boone explicó más tarde que Bellinger también estaba notando el estrés acumulado por la superficie sintética y que no quería aumentar la carga sobre él.
Esa cautela se mantuvo durante todo el partido, que los Yankees acabaron perdiendo por un jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith en la novena entrada. También fue importante porque Nueva York está a punto de marcharse de Arizona para afrontar una serie crucial de cuatro partidos contra Tampa Bay en el Yankee Stadium, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada en la que se repartirán las victorias. Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el equipo sigue buscando el equilibrio entre la lucha por el título de división y mantener intacta su plantilla para octubre.
La preocupación por el estado del césped dejó de ser un simple detalle de gestión de la alineación en cuanto Boone explicó por qué faltaba otro titular. Los Yankees habían llegado a un punto en el que un pie lesionado más podía complicar tanto su alineación en los jardines como la profundidad de plantilla que podrían necesitar durante la última semana.
Ese cálculo es especialmente importante en el centro del campo, donde Boone tiene menos combinaciones con las que está acostumbrado a trabajar una vez que empieza a proteger a los jugadores de las lesiones. Un ajuste de una sola noche puede convertirse rápidamente en un problema para la plantilla si las molestias persisten de cara a la recta final de la temporada.
Jones se queda fuera tras un repunte del dolor en el talón al jugar sobre césped artificial
Spencer Jones no jugó el sábado por unas molestias en el pie izquierdo y el talón, después de haberse dado un golpe en el talón a principios de semana en Minnesota. Jones dijo que las molestias se agravaron por el desgaste de haber jugado el viernes por la noche en el césped del Chase Field.
El novato restó importancia al tema antes del partido y dijo que esperaba que la baja durara solo un día.
«No es nada grave», dijo Jones.
Jones describió el problema como una molestia más que como una nueva lesión aguda. También lo relacionó directamente con la superficie y con los impactos que habían absorbido sus pies.
«Solo estoy un poco magullado», dijo Jones. «Jugar sobre césped artificial es diferente, es duro para los pies».
Boone dijo que la situación de Jones se evaluaría día a día y que estuvo a punto de dejarlo en la alineación. También dejó claro que los Yankees no consideraban que Jones estuviera fuera de combate.
«Simplemente me pareció que, sobre todo al estar aquí en el césped artificial, se había dado un golpe en el talón en Minnesota y, al volver a jugar en césped [el viernes], creo que es algo que hay que valorar día a día», dijo Boone. «Incluso creo que podría jugar esta noche».
Las declaraciones de Boone tras el partido son lo que más tranquilidad dan
Jones no llegó a salir en el partido del sábado, pero Boone dijo después que la decisión se debió más a la situación del partido que a motivos médicos. El entrenador dijo que habría sacado a Jones si los Yankees hubieran tenido el enfrentamiento adecuado o lo hubieran necesitado al final del partido.
«Estaba disponible, igual que yo lo habría estado… si hubiera surgido una oportunidad de batear o hubiéramos tenido que hacer algo, habría recurrido a él», dijo Boone.
Esa distinción es importante. A Jones no le han dado de baja, ni lo han puesto en la lista de lesionados, ni le han prohibido hacer nada relacionado con el béisbol. El domingo por la mañana, los Yankees seguían considerando el problema como una molestia pasajera.
La profundidad en el centro del campo hace que un día de descanso cobre más importancia
Los Yankees pueden permitirse que se pierda un solo partido. La situación de la plantilla se complica si Jones necesita más tiempo.
Jones ha jugado 80 partidos esta temporada y tiene un promedio de bateo de .248, con un porcentaje de embasado de .318 y un porcentaje de slugging de .433. Lleva 10 jonrones, 12 dobles, un triple, 38 carreras impulsadas y nueve bases robadas en 265 turnos al bate. Baseball Savant le atribuye 23 hits de más de una base, es decir, uno cada 11,5 turnos al bate.
Su valía también se nota en cómo los Yankees pueden colocar al resto del equipo. Caballero puede jugar de central, pero el sábado fue solo su segunda titularidad en esa posición esta temporada. Boone decidió expresamente no cambiar a Bellinger al centro por culpa del césped artificial y de la propia carga de trabajo de Bellinger.
Los Yankees también llamaron a Max Schuemann cuando Judge entró en la lista de lesionados, dando prioridad a la versatilidad defensiva. Esa decisión le da a Boone otra opción en todas las posiciones del campo y en los jardines, pero no sustituye la potencia de Jones como bateador zurdo ni su papel habitual en el centro del campo.
Los Yankees llegan a la última jornada de la serie con una duda sobre su estado físico
Los Yankees cierran la serie contra Arizona el domingo, antes del día de descanso del lunes. Ese descanso le da a Jones un poco más de tiempo para recuperarse antes de los cuatro partidos contra los Rays en tres días en el Yankee Stadium.
Por ahora, el último informe médico sigue siendo alentador. Jones espera que las molestias sean pasajeras, Boone lo consideraba apto para jugar el sábado y el club no ha dado a entender que se esté planteando incluirlo en la lista de lesionados.
La pregunta que queda es si un día de descanso del césped del Chase Field será suficiente para que el talón se recupere antes de que los Yankees empiecen la serie más importante que les queda en el calendario de la temporada regular.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.content:encoded:
Fans slammed Yankees rookie SS George Lombard Jr. for his defensive error in Saturday night's game against the Diamondbacks at Chase Field. In the bottom of the seventh, with the game tied 3-3, Lombard dropped an easy infield grounder, allowing D-backs pinch hitter Ildemaro Vargas to reach first base on an error.
While the home side failed to score a run in that inning, fans expressed their displeasure with Lombard's error on social media.
Watch the video here:
Here are some fan reactions:
"Time to get him out of the lineup," one fan commented.
Lombard Jr. went 0-for-4 to end the night as the Yankees lost the contest 5-3, despite a strong start from ace Cam Schlittler and home runs from Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells.
George Lombard Jr. Continues to Make a Positive Impact Despite Some Errors
Lombard Jr. has been a little careless on defense in recent games, which understandably raises concerns among fans. But despite the infield errors, the rookie SS has made a positive impact since joining the roster a day after the trade deadline.
In 36 games this season, the 21-year-old has compiled a .227 batting average, with four home runs, 15 RBIs, and a .643 OPS.
While the Yankee faithful and the front office might have some doubts about his postseason fortunes, Lombard Jr. is sure to come in handy in the batting lineup as the Yankees attempt to adjust their lineup and choose players carefully, with captain Aaron Judge sidelined until September 27 and the Wild Card series starting on September 29.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] What the Yankees' Lineup Should Look Like Without Aaron Judge In October
item.dc:creator: Michael Zeno; Unknown
item.description: Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be. A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be. A scenario is now potentially unfo
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge's regular season may be over, but that doesn't mean the Yankees' has to be.
A mystery calf ailment popped up suddenly on Wednesday and has resulted in the Yankees captain being placed on the injured list. It's unclear whether he will return in 2026, even if he's eligible to return next weekend. Aaron Boone did not give any information on the severity of the calf issue, but the timeline is likely not good due to how tricky those injuries prove to be.
A scenario is now potentially unfolding that would have only appeared in Boone's nightmares: a postseason without the best hitter in baseball, with a lineup that struggled mightily without him. Even if they seemed to gradually improve as time went on, particularly in August, it would be a massive blow if he cannot return.
You can't replace a guy like Judge midseason; you can merely do your best to make up for his absence. Fortunately, on a platoon-heavy team like this, they should have plenty of options to build a lineup without him for the playoffs.
What the playoff lineup should look like against right-handed pitching
- Ben Rice (DH)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Luis García Jr. (1B)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Austin Wells (C)
- Ryan McMahon (3B)
This lineup simultaneously features the easiest decisions, but also the roughest circumstances. Having a guy like Judge as the ultimate lineup balancer who mashed both lefties and righties allowed you to use plenty of left-handed hitters at the top of the order, something that the team has in abundance.
The best right-handed hitter on the roster without Judge is hard to pinpoint, especially since all of them are significantly worse against same-handed pitching. Heliot Ramos might just be the best option to bat highest among them, which would be cleanup in this scenario.
It's not an ideal situation in the slightest. Even if you don't think it makes sense to bat Ramos that high because of his struggles against righties, there is some merit to breaking up the team's many left-handed bats. In a lineup that will likely only feature one other righty, it has to be considered.
The fate of this lineup when they're out there, which would likely be mostly after a potential Wild Card Series with the Red Sox, would hinge on the middle. Spencer Jones and Jazz Chisholm Jr. got hot in August and helped the offensive turnaround begin, but both are heavily streaky bats with contact issues. If they go cold, this lineup might limp through games like they did in July.
What the playoff lineup should look like against left-handed pitching
- Paul Goldschmidt (1B)
- Cody Bellinger (LF)
- Heliot Ramos (RF)
- Ben Rice (DH)
- George Lombard Jr. (SS)
- Spencer Jones (CF)
- Jazz Chisholm Jr. (2B)
- Anthony Volpe/José Caballero (3B)
- Austin Wells (C)
Here's where it gets interesting. How far do you lean into the platoons on a team with several players designated to specifically hit lefties, especially against a team that will likely lean heavily on those types of pitchers in Boston?
Many Yankees fans believe that it would be improper to take a guy like García, who is likely the team's second-best pound-for-pound hitter with Judge injured, out of the lineup, but you don't really have a choice here. He's slashing just .238/.274/.363 against lefties, while Goldschmidt has been among the team's best hitters against them for the last two seasons. Add in Rice's improvements against same-handed pitching, and it just needs to be done.
Using him in a different position is also just not happening. He has not played second base, where he was extremely poor, since 2025. The only position he's played this season is first base. If he wasn't so dreadful out there, maybe he could replace Chisholm, a mediocre hitter against lefties in his own right.
Speaking of defense, you might notice the lack of Amed Rosario, and that's intentional. Rosario's use on this roster was almost exclusively predicated on his ability to hit left-handed pitching, but he's been significantly worse at it this season. Add in his truly dreadful defense, and you have a conundrum.
Anthony Volpe is a better hitter than José Caballero, but there are questions about how his arm strength would play at third, where he's also very inexperienced with just three games played in Triple-A. Caballero would probably get the nod here, but he's someone who just plays better off the bench with his speed and versatility.
It's also an aggressive placement for Lombard, batting fifth in his first career playoff game. The results haven't quite been there yet for him, but he's always been significantly better against lefties and should be slid up the lineup and be treated as one of those platoon bats who are there to hit that handedness, even if it might lead to consequences in the bullpen.
Boston is loaded with left-handed pitching from the rotation to the bullpen, so there will be few opportunities to get to a guy like García on the bench. The rest of the bench would be situational with pinch runners and pinch hitters.
Things ultimately look particularly shallow, but is there a chance that some last-minute reinforcements could help out?
Could Trent Grisham or Giancarlo Stanton return to provide relief?
It seems unlikely, especially early in the postseason, but the Yankees are refusing to shut the door on either Trent Grisham's or Giancarlo Stanton's return.
Grisham, who suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain earlier this month, was revealed to be "pretty far along" in his running program, and Boone said it's not out of the question that he returns in the season's final days, although an exact timeline for that has not been spelled out. If Grisham is physically ready to get back on the field, it would provide a boost, even if he might not be starting over Jones at this point.
Stanton, who's been out since April due to two separate calf strains and a re-aggravation, has continued to hit through his rehab, but hasn't resumed running as of last Sunday. Considering how it took several weeks for him to even get close to back from injury with his running program last time, this likely doesn't put him in play until the ALCS at the earliest.
While Stanton seems significantly less likely to get into a game again this season, there is a path for Grisham. The team could use him and Ramos in a platoon situation to add yet another lefty to the lineup against right-handed pitching. They could also utilize him as a pinch hitter on a larger bench than usual, due to the team's propensity to carry fewer than 13 pitchers in the Wild Card Series.
The real question for Grisham is defensive. While Jones has absolutely looked shaky in center field, the struggles of Grisham out there are well documented. Add in his diminished athleticism and likely balky hamstring straight off an injury, would it be better if the team just chanced it by throwing him in right field when he plays?
He hasn't played the position since a disastrous error lost the Brewers the 2019 Wild Card Game against the Nationals, but playing it at Yankee Stadium is significantly easier than dealing with the spacious center field. Of course, this is something the Yankees would have to determine their willingness to do beforehand and have him practice the position, so what plans they have will be determined by that.
As for Stanton if he's ever medically able to get back? There just might not be any room for him with Rice as the permanent DH. You don't want to take the bat out of either of their hands, and with the team seemingly having to juggle multiple guys coming off soft-tissue injuries, can they afford to use a roster spot for a designated pinch hitter as they did with 2022 Matt Carpenter?

item.content:encoded:
The St. Louis Cardinals missed the playoffs this season and will need to head back to the drawing board to build a team that can qualify for the postseason next year.
Moreover, the question is what moves they should make to improve the team to challenge the Chicago Cubs and Milwaukee Brewers in the NL Central.
It’s been a wild 2026 MLB season for Anthony Volpe, who was optioned to Triple-A in August and then recalled in September. Still, it might be in the 25-year-old’s best interest to get a fresh start elsewhere.
Since reaching the majors in 2023, Volpe has been hitting .225 with 432 hits, 54 homers, 218 RBIs, and 241 runs scored in 537 games for the New York Yankees in his career, per StatMuse.
Despite this production during his four seasons in Pinstripes, FanSided’s Robert Murray believes that the Cardinals could be the change of scenery that Volpe needs after a rollercoaster career with the Yankees.
“Anthony Volpe would be a really good, buy-low option for the Cardinals,” Murray wrote in a Sept. 19 article. “Volpe was supposed to be the Yankees’ long-term answer at shortstop. Instead, he struggled mightily and fluctuated between the majors and minors.
“The Yankees still believe in Volpe and want to hold him, so a trade might be considered unlikely. But this is something that other teams will sniff around this offseason, I believe, and Bloom – who has previously worked with the Red Sox and Rays – should have plenty of familiarity in dealing with the Yankees.”
Anthony Volpe Could Boost Trade Value In the Coming Weeks
Since being recalled on Sept. 9, Volpe has performed well. Entering Sept. 20, Volpe has been batting .290 with nine hits, a home run, seven RBIs, and four runs scored in seven games, per StatMuse.
Moreover, if Volpe can end the season on a high note and have a productive postseason, his trade value might increase, and a team like the Cardinals could feel they can tap into his potential.
Volpe will have an opportunity to step up like every Yankee in that lineup, given that Aaron Judge is back on the injured list. New York can’t replace Judge with one batter, but they can do so with everyone chipping in.
Cardinals, Yankees Get Compelling Trade Idea
Recently, Christopher Kline of FanSided floated a trade idea that would send Volpe along with LHP Brent Headrick and LHP Kyle Carr to the Cardinals for 24-year-old shortstop Masyn Winn.
“The Yankees’ lack of fundamental soundness on the defensive end has bitten them in the you-know-what all season, just like it did last year,” Kline wrote in a Sept. 16 article. “The hope was that top prospect George Lombard Jr. could steady the ship at shortstop, but he has stacked up errors left and right.
“It’s too early to write off the 21-year-old long term, but he could serve more comfortably at third or second — which is notable, since Jazz Chisholm Jr. is about to [be a free agent]. Winn immediately alleviates a ton of defensive issues for the Yankees, while his weaker bat would be well-protected in the American League’s most potent lineup.”

item.content:encoded:
Los New York Yankees respondieron con autoridad en su primer partido sin Aaron Judge y derrotaron 9-2 a los Arizona Diamondbacks este viernes en Chase Field. Nueva York fabricó cinco carreras en la primera entrada, Ben Rice y George Lombard Jr. conectaron cuadrangulares y Gerrit Cole lanzó seis entradas de calidad para llevarse una victoria que también tuvo un significado histórico para el derecho.
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Aaron Judge vuelve a la lista de lesionados de los Yankees!
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
La jornada comenzó con una noticia importante para los Yankees: Judge fue colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Sin su principal figura ofensiva, Nueva York necesitó encontrar producción desde el primer turno y la respuesta llegó inmediatamente frente al abridor de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez.
Los primeros cinco bateadores de los Yankees lograron embasarse. Ben Rice recibió una base por bolas y posteriormente Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor para abrir la pizarra. Después llegaron más oportunidades para la ofensiva neoyorquina, hasta que George Lombard Jr. conectó un sencillo de dos carreras que llevó el marcador a 5-0 antes de que terminara el primer episodio. Rodríguez necesitó 45 lanzamientos para conseguir los tres outs de la entrada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera en un primer inning.
Arizona intentó reaccionar en el segundo capítulo. Corbin Carroll conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras para acercar a los Diamondbacks a 5-2 y darle algo de vida al público de Chase Field. Sin embargo, Cole logró contener la ofensiva local y evitó que la reacción se transformara en una amenaza mayor.
La respuesta de los Yankees llegó en la tercera entrada. Ben Rice volvió a aparecer y conectó un cuadrangular solitario, su número 39 de la temporada, para recuperar la diferencia de cuatro carreras y colocar el encuentro 6-2. El batazo también completó una noche ofensiva sobresaliente para Rice, quien terminó con dos imparables, dos bases por bolas, dos carreras y dos carreras impulsadas.
Mientras la ofensiva seguía produciendo, Cole encontró estabilidad desde la lomita. Después del cuadrangular de Carroll, el derecho no permitió otra carrera y completó seis entradas con cuatro hits, dos carreras limpias, ninguna base por bolas y seis ponches. Venía de dos aperturas en las que había permitido siete jonrones combinados, por lo que su actuación en Phoenix representó una recuperación importante en su temporada.
Lombard Jr. volvió a aparecer en la sexta entrada. El campocorto conectó su tercer jonrón de la temporada, esta vez solitario, para ampliar la ventaja de Nueva York a 7-2. El joven infielder terminó la noche con dos imparables y tres carreras impulsadas, convirtiéndose en otra de las figuras ofensivas del triunfo visitante.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
Los Yankees agregaron dos carreras más en la séptima entrada para terminar de sentenciar el encuentro. La ofensiva visitante terminó con ocho hits y nueve carreras, mientras que Arizona consiguió siete imparables, pero no volvió a pisar el plato después del segundo inning.
Para Cole, la victoria tuvo un valor especial. El derecho llegó a 162 triunfos en su carrera, superando a Mike Moore y convirtiéndose en el lanzador con más victorias entre los jugadores que fueron seleccionados con el primer pick global del Draft. Cole fue elegido por los Pittsburgh Pirates con la primera selección en 2011.
La derrota, en cambio, complicó todavía más el panorama de Arizona en la recta final de la temporada. Los Diamondbacks llegaron al encuentro buscando mantenerse en la pelea por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, pero la caída ante Nueva York significó su tercera derrota consecutiva. Al término de la jornada quedaron cinco juegos por detrás del último puesto de Wild Card, con ocho encuentros restantes.
Los Yankees, ya clasificados a los playoffs, mejoraron a 89-64 y se colocaron a cuatro juegos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con nueve partidos por disputar. Nueva York además consiguió su octava victoria en sus últimos 10 encuentros.
El triunfo llegó, además, en una noche en la que los Yankees tuvieron que afrontar la ausencia de Judge. Rice y Lombard Jr. aportaron los batazos largos, mientras que Cole respondió desde el montículo para que Nueva York tomara el primer partido de la serie en Arizona con una victoria contundente de 9-2.

item.dc:creator: Cole Sullivan

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees secured a 9-2 series-opening victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
Now, they're once again back in action on Saturday evening with right-handed ace and AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler on the mound for the Yankees, while the Diamondbacks will have righty Brandon Pfaadt pitching.
Ahead of the matchup, manager Aaron Boone didn't make any major changes to his starting lineup, but he did make some notable changes to his batting order.
Yankees Announce George Lombard Jr. Move
With outfielder Spencer Jones getting the day off and veteran Paul Goldschmidt out of the lineup after leading off on Friday, rookie shortstop George Lombard Jr. is moving up in the batting order.
After hitting seventh in the series opener, Boone is placing Lombard Jr. in the five-hole Saturday, while Heliot Ramos bats cleanup and Ben Rice moves back into the leadoff role.
Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. will remain in their normal roles, hitting second and third.
Here's the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: "Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP."
Yankees 9/19
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
L. García Jr. 1B
H. Ramos RF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
R. McMahon 3B
J. Caballero CF
C. Schlittler SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 19, 2026
Lombard Jr.'s 2026 Season
Since the Yankees called him up on Aug. 4, Lombard Jr. has exceeded expectations and made an immediate impact for New York.
He's appeared in 35 games and has gone 29-for-124 with 19 runs, four home runs, and 15 RBIs while hitting .234 with a .371 slugging percentage and a .663 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Saturday with an 89-64 overall record and currently holds the top Wild Card spot, which would set them up to host a Wild Card series at home in the Bronx.
That said, they're just 4.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East and the No. 1 overall seed in the AL, with an upcoming four-game set against the Rays this week.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are in the middle of a three-game series against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field in Phoenix.
New York won the first game of the series 9-2 on Friday. Game 2 is slated to begin at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday.
Before Saturday’s game, the Yankees announced a surprising lineup decision involving José Caballero.
New York Yankees Announce Interesting José Caballero Decision
Surprisingly, José Caballero will start in center field for the Yankees on Saturday. Caballero has played 11 innings in center this season and recorded 15 innings at the position last year.
Meanwhile, Spencer Jones, the Yankees’ primary center fielder, is out of the lineup with a sore left foot.
The New York Post’s Greg Joyce wrote on X: Spencer Jones said he’s dealing with a sore left foot, which he chalked up to the wear-and-tear from playing on turf. But downplayed it, said he’s fine, just getting a day. “It’s no big deal,” Jones said.
Here is the Yankees’ full lineup for Saturday:
- Ben Rice DH
- Cody Bellinger LF
- Luis Garcia Jr. 1B
- Heliot Ramos RF
- George Lombard Jr. SS
- Austin Wells C
- Anthony Volpe 2B
- Ryan McMahon 3B
- José Caballero CF
Starting Pitcher: RHP Cam Schlittler
Here is the Diamondbacks’ lineup:
- Laars Nootbar LF
- Ketel Marte 2B
- Gabriel Moreon C
- Geraldo Perdomo SS
- Corbin Carroll RF
- Nolan Arenado 3B
- Tim Tawa 1B
- Jesus Sanchez DH
- Jordan Lawlar CF
Starting Pitcher: Brandon Pfaadt
New York Yankees Right Now
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] How the Yankees Should Utilize Jazz Chisholm Jr. When He Returns
item.dc:creator: Joe Najarian; Unknown

One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. item.content:encoded:
With Aaron Judge likely done for the season, the New York Yankees will rely heavily on their other bats to pick up the slack.
One of those will be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is nearing a return from the injured list with a sprained right thumb. Chisholm, who was putting up an .832 OPS and .367 wOBA since August 4, is expected to be activated during the Yankees' final homestand this coming week. Despite a very disappointing season as a whole, the 28-year-old's improved play is an extremely encouraging sign.
At the same time, Anthony Volpe has taken full advantage of his new opportunity at second base. When Chisholm went down, Volpe's improvements at the plate in Triple-A carried over to the major leagues and his production from the bottom of the order is a boon to the Yankees' offense. The 25-year old is slashing .296/.345/.481 in 29 plate appearances while also stealing four bases.
The problem is that the Yankees have three middle infielders looking for starting spots. George Lombard Jr. is firmly entrenched at shortstop, which necessitated Volpe's transition to second base. Of course, second base is Chisholm's natural position and the Yankees have gotten well-above average defense from him there.
This means one of these three will be the odd man out... or does it?
The Yankees should play Jazz Chisholm Jr. at third base again
When the Yankees acquired Chisholm at the trade deadline in 2024, they already had Gleyber Torres at second base. So they tested Chisholm out at third base to ensure both players would be in the starting lineup. Chisholm also saw time at the hot corner last year when DJ LeMahieu played second, until the Yankees eventually released the aging LeMahieu to move Chisholm back to his natural position.
Chisholm's defense suffered at third in 2025, as he was worth -3 Outs Above Average (per Baseball Savant). But his athleticism and dynamic skillset is far too great to leave him out of the lineup entirely, even if he's endured a down year. On the other hand, it would be foolish for the Yankees to sit Volpe while he's hot at the plate and adapting well to second.
While second base has two strong options, third base is a major weakness. Ryan McMahon has been atrocious since returning to the lineup on Sept. 1, hitting just .154/.214/.179 in 42 plate appearances; the abysmal offensive production far outweighs McMahon's steady defense, even if the Yankees are going to rely on run prevention in the postseason. Jose Caballero is also capable of playing third, but he's best suited as a bench player at this point.
Between Chisholm and Volpe, the former is better suited to play third due to his past experience. The latter has a grand total of three games and 22.0 innings at the hot corner, all of them in Triple-A.
This certainly isn't an ideal situation for Chisholm: he's struggled for much of the season, got injured when he started turning things around, and may need to play at a secondary position to accommodate a teammate.
But this would likely be the Yankees' best lineup without Aaron Judge, and if Chisholm wants to both win a World Series and secure a future in the Bronx, then moving over to third is the best thing he can do to help the team right now.
Joe Najarian is a writer for Yankees On SI, having previously covered the Yankees both for SI and additional sites since 2023. He also served as Deputy Editor for the Yankees, Mets and Orioles On SI sites, and additionally contributes to Athlon Sports and Men’s Journal covering Major League Baseball and other trending sports news. Joe is a graduate of Rutgers University in 2022, earning a bachelor’s degree in Journalism and Media Studies.
Follow JoeNajarian

item.title: [CBS Sports] Three questions for Aaron Judge and the Yankees as injury casts doubt on slugger's playoff availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
